lines.sentence: The night stretched on above, as the stars and moon lit the way of the hostess and bard, like a path toward a desolate city.
Wow. You know, when you talked about going to a temple of the sun, I expected something a little more populated.
So did I…
…Why are we here again, dear taverness?
Remember the disruptive customer of a few weeks ago?
“Bruster”, yes?
He spoke of getting a “lay of the land”. None see as much as the Sun.
Ha! I believe you may have been overthinking his advice! That or we’re trusting the word of a drunk. Or both…
The sand and limestone that set the silent streets were cool with the temperature of night. At the end of the road lies a massive obelisk with a falcon on its tip.
Iunu. Heliopolis.
Ahem, Ms. Laurel? I wanted to ask you about our disruptive alcoholic. You see, something he mentioned keeps ringing in my head, and I feel that you-
Come all! For the night is getting old! Watch as I raise the sun back from the Underworld! I shall give a passionate khutbah!
Ugh…
Ms. Laurel! Are you alright? Are the headaches getting to you again?
Y-yeah…
... I think… we shouldn’t have come here…
Nonsense, any reason you had to come here had to have been a good one. Here, let me help you up. Please be strong enough to let it pass.
Are you alright, newcomers? The khutbah is going to start soon! I’m sure I can get my granddaughter Isis to heal any sicknesses you feel.
Strae… it's him.
Well, this is quite rude of you, the God of the Sun deserves some respect no? Fall and bow to his excellence.
Shadows of people start to surround the two. Forms. Silhouettes. Dozens, or hundreds of hands reach to take, to heal.
No, those lies… don't let him… Stall him…
